title: Febris client software distribution manifest
description: Index of published client-software artifacts (mobile Server APK, mobile Companion APK, PC launcher installer, integration SDKs). Consumed by a node's package-feed sync and readable by a human. Designed to map one-to-one onto the node's LocalSoftwarePackage catalog row so the sync is a field copy rather than a translation. See docs/OSS_CLIENT_DISTRIBUTION.md.

schemaVersion.description: Bumped only on a BREAKING change to this document's shape. Consumers must refuse a schemaVersion they do not know rather than guess.

generated.description: UTC timestamp this manifest was produced. Informational only: never use it to decide which package is newest, because a regenerated manifest does not mean a new release.

packages.description: Every published artifact still worth advertising, including obsolete ones. Order carries no meaning; a consumer that needs newest-first must sort by versionCode itself.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256, matching the casing the node's PackageArtifact.Sha256 records so the two are directly comparable.

uuid.description: STABLE identity of this release, assigned by the publisher and never reused. This is what makes a re-sync idempotent: the node upserts its catalog row keyed on this UUID, so ingesting the same release twice updates one row instead of creating two. It is also the id a client later downloads by.

kind.description: Human-readable artifact kind. Mirrors the LocalSoftwarePackageType member name.

kindId.description: The LocalSoftwarePackageType integer value, carried alongside the name so no consumer has to maintain a name-to-enum mapping that can silently drift. A consumer MUST treat a kind/kindId disagreement as a fatal manifest error.

name.description: Display name for catalogs and download pages.

version.description: Human-facing version, SemVer. Free-form as far as Android is concerned; versionCode is what the platform actually enforces.

versionCode.description: Android's monotonically increasing upgrade counter, derived as MAJOR*10000 + MINOR*100 + PATCH. REQUIRED for the two Android kinds and meaningless for the others. Must match the value compiled into the APK: a mismatch is undetectable by the node and produces an install that silently disagrees with the catalog.

channel.description: Release channel. A node syncs one channel and ignores the rest.

consumers.description: WHO is expected to fetch this, which is not the same for every kind and is enforced elsewhere in the product. AndroidMobileServer is ["human","node"] because it is the bootstrap: a tablet with no Febris app cannot fetch its own first app, so a person must be able to click it. AndroidMobileCompanion is ["node"] only, matching the developer portal deliberately refusing to serve it to a browser and instead letting the mobile Server pull it and install it over ADB. A consumer that ignores this field still works, so it is documentation with teeth rather than a gate.

language.description: LanguageMapTypeEnum member name. Optional; a consumer defaults it when absent.

packageName.description: Android application id. PERMANENT once published, on the same footing as the signing key: it cannot change without every user uninstalling and losing local data. Android kinds only.

obsolete.description: Mirrors the node catalog's own Obsolete flag, so "latest non-obsolete" resolves identically on both sides. Superseded releases stay listed rather than being deleted, so an operator can still fetch an older build deliberately.

artifact.description: The downloadable unit. A .zip wrapping the payload for every kind except CSharp, because the deployed mobile client already downloads and writes a .zip and preserving that envelope means no mobile-side change. The CSharp kind (400) alone may be a .nupkg: its canonical artifact IS the published NuGet package (zip-format internally), and wrapping it again would create a second artifact nobody publishes.

url.description: Direct download URL. Anonymous and unauthenticated by design.

sha256.description: Checksum of the ZIP as served. A consumer MUST verify this BEFORE committing the artifact to its catalog, or a truncated download becomes a published package.

contains.description: What is inside the zip. Lets a consumer verify the payload rather than only its wrapper.

signerSha256.description: SHA-256 of the APK SIGNING CERTIFICATE, not of the file. This is the only field here that proves ORIGIN rather than integrity: a public URL plus a public checksum authenticates that bytes arrived intact and says nothing about who produced them. A node that pins this value can refuse an artifact signed by anyone else. Obtain it with `apksigner verify --print-certs`.

releaseNotes.description: URL of the human-readable notes for this release.

allOf.description: The Android kinds must carry the platform fields that only mean something for them.
Only the CSharp kind (400) may ship a .nupkg artifact -- that IS its canonical published unit; every other kind stays .zip.
